paragraphs: We incorporated as Helen of Troy Corporation in Texas in 1968 and were reorganized as Helen of Troy Limited in Bermuda in 1994. We are a leading global consumer products company offering creative products and solutions for our customers through a diversified portfolio of brands. We have built leading market positions through new product innovation, product quality and competitive pricing. We go to market under a number of brands, some of which are licensed. Our portfolio of brands includes OXO, Hydro Flask, Osprey, Vicks, Braun, Honeywell, PUR, Hot Tools, Drybar, Curlsmith, Revlon and Olive & June, among others.
We currently operate in two reportable business segments:

•Home & Outdoor: Offers a broad range of outstanding world-class brands that help consumers enjoy everyday living inside their homes and outdoors. Our innovative products for home activities include food preparation and storage, cooking, cleaning, organization and beverage service. Our outdoor performance range, on-the-go food storage and beverageware includes lifestyle hydration products, coolers and food storage solutions, backpacks and travel gear. Sales for this global segment are primarily to online and brick & mortar retailers and through our direct-to-consumer channel.

•Beauty & Wellness: Provides consumers with a broad range of outstanding world-class brands for beauty and wellness. In Beauty, we deliver innovation through products such as hair styling appliances, grooming tools, liquid and aerosol personal care products and nail care solutions that help consumers look and feel more beautiful. In Wellness, we are there when you need us most with highly regarded humidifiers, thermometers, water and air purifiers, heaters and fans. Sales for this global segment are primarily to online and brick & mortar retailers, distributors and through our direct-to-consumer channel.
For more segment and geographic information concerning our net sales revenue, long-lived assets and operating income, refer to Note 17 to the accompanying consolidated financial statements.

During fiscal 2026, we made significant organizational and operational changes designed to stabilize our business. The Board of Directors appointed a new Chief Executive Officer with transformation experience needed to help drive our next phase of value creation. Under this new leadership, we are currently engaged in a comprehensive review of our strategic priorities as we re-position our Company to deliver sustained revenue and profit growth, increase market share and create superior long-term value for all stakeholders.

We are taking steps to modernize our business model designed to move at the speed of the consumer and excel in a rapidly evolving environment with fragmented consumer attention and shifting value perceptions. Our strategy includes the following priorities: reenergize our brands and our people, adapt our organizational structure to put the consumer at the center of everything we do, strengthen our brand portfolio for predictable long-term growth, and improve asset efficiency. As part of our strategy, we plan to sharpen our focus on fewer, more impactful initiatives, which include investing more in product innovation, strengthening brand loyalty, and advancing commercial excellence. We intend to energize our brands through a disciplined investment approach focusing on impactful opportunities that generate competitive advantages and deliver product solutions and world-class innovation to our consumers. In

addition, we believe our consumer-centric approach will enable us to better understand our consumers, allocate resources more efficiently, and accelerate the time to market for new products and brands with the best opportunities for long-term sustainable growth. We expect this will strengthen our portfolio of brands to provide a pathway for strong cash flow generation to further invest back into our business. We remain focused on improving balance sheet health and productivity, by prioritizing our capital expenditures, optimizing our working capital, and monetizing less productive assets. While we are finalizing this strategy reset, we have already implemented many of the foundational changes intended to drive long-term performance, and we have taken immediate actions we believe will accelerate our product innovation, sharpen our go-to-market execution, strengthen our cash flow, and pay down our debt.

headings: We rely on licensed trademarks from third parties and license certain trademarks to third parties in exchange for royalty income, the loss of which could have a material adverse effect on our revenues and profitability.
To compete successfully, we must develop and introduce a continuing stream of innovative new products to meet changing consumer preferences.
Large customers may take actions that adversely affect our gross profit and operating results.

Our operating results are dependent on sales to several large customers and the loss of, or substantial decline in, sales to a top customer could have a material adverse effect on our revenues and profitability.
Our ability to deliver products to our customers in a timely manner and to satisfy our customers' fulfillment standards are subject to several factors, some of which are beyond our control.

Our business is subject to weather conditions, the duration and severity of the cold and flu season and other related factors, which can cause our operating results to vary from quarter to quarter and year to year.
We rely on our CEO and a limited number of other key senior officers to operate our business. The loss of any of these individuals could have a material adverse effect on our business.

Changes in laws and regulations, including environmental, employment and health and safety and tax laws, and the costs and complexities of compliance with such laws could have a material adverse impact on our business.

Increased focus and expectations on climate change and other sustainability matters could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations and damage our reputation.
Significant changes in or our compliance with regulations, interpretations or product certification requirements could adversely impact our operations.
Global legal developments regarding privacy and data security could result in changes to our business practices, penalties, increased cost of operations, or otherwise harm our business.

Our business involves the potential for product recalls, product liability and other claims against us, which could materially and adversely affect our business, operating results and financial condition.
paragraphs: Carefully consider the risks described below and all of the other information included in our Annual Report when deciding whether to invest in our securities or otherwise evaluating our business. If any of the risks or other events or circumstances described elsewhere in this Annual Report materialize, our business, operating results or financial condition may suffer. As a result, the trading price of our common stock and the value of your investment might significantly decline. The risks listed below are not the only risks that we face. Additional risks unknown to us or that we currently believe are insignificant may also affect our business.

You should also refer to the explanation of the qualifications and limitations on forward-looking statements under "Information Regarding Forward-Looking Statements," at the end of Item 7., "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations." All forward-looking statements made by us are qualified by the risk factors described below.
The following is a summary of some of the principal risk factors which are more fully described below.
•The geographic concentration of certain of our U.S. distribution facilities increases our risk to disruptions that could affect our ability to deliver products in a timely manner.

•The occurrence of cyber incidents, or failure by us or our third-party service providers to maintain cybersecurity and the integrity of confidential internal or customer data, could have a material adverse effect on our operations and profitability.

•A cybersecurity breach, obsolescence or interruptions in the operation of our central global Enterprise Resource Planning systems and other peripheral information systems could have a material adverse effect on our operations and profitability.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") should be read in conjunction with the other sections of this Annual Report, including Item 1., "Business" and Item 8., "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data." The various sections of this MD&A contain a number of forward-looking statements, all of which are based on our current expectations. Actual results may differ materially due to a number of factors, including those discussed in Item 1A.,"Risk Factors," and in the section entitled "Information Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" following this MD&A, and in Item 7A., "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk."

Management uses the following key financial measures, some of which are non-GAAP, as further described below: net sales revenue, organic business sales revenue, adjusted operating margin and adjusted diluted earnings per share ("EPS"). Management uses these measures to evaluate historical performance on a comparable basis, predict future performance and benchmark our performance against our competitors. We believe these measures provide management and investors with important information that is useful in understanding our business results and trends.

This MD&A, including the tables under the headings "Operating (Loss) Income, Operating Margin, Adjusted Operating Income (non-GAAP) and Adjusted Operating Margin (non-GAAP) by Segment" and "Net (Loss) Income, Diluted (Loss) Earnings Per Share, Adjusted Income (non-GAAP) and Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share (non-GAAP)," reports operating (loss) income, operating margin, net (loss) income and diluted (loss) earnings per share without the impact of acquisition-related expenses, asset impairment charges, a discrete tax charge to revalue existing deferred tax liabilities due to Barbados enacting domestic corporate income tax legislation ("Barbados tax reform"), costs incurred in connection with the departure of our former Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") primarily related to severance and recruitment costs ("CEO succession costs"), settlement costs related to EPA packaging and labeling compliance for certain products in the air filtration, water filtration and humidification categories ("EPA compliance costs"), a transitional income tax benefit resulting from the recognition of deferred tax assets in connection with the reorganization of our intangible assets in fiscal 2025 and income tax expense from the recognition of valuation allowances in fiscal 2026 on the related deferred tax assets ("intangible asset reorganization"), restructuring charges, amortization of intangible assets and non-cash share-based compensation for the periods presented, as applicable. These measures may be considered non-GAAP financial measures as defined by SEC Regulation G, Rule 100. The tables reconcile these measures to their corresponding GAAP-based financial measures presented in our consolidated statements of (loss) income. We believe that adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted income and adjusted diluted earnings per share provide useful information to management and investors regarding financial and business trends relating to our financial condition and results of operations. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures, in combination with our financial results calculated in accordance with GAAP, provide investors with additional perspective regarding the impact of such charges and benefits on applicable income, margin and earnings per share measures. We also believe that these non-GAAP measures reflect the operating performance of our business and facilitate a more direct comparison of our performance to our competitors. The material limitation associated with the use of the non-GAAP financial measures is that the non-GAAP measures do not reflect the full economic impact of our activities. Our adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted income and adjusted diluted earnings per share are not prepared in accordance with GAAP, are not an alternative to GAAP financial measures and may be calculated differently than non-GAAP financial measures disclosed by other companies. Accordingly, undue reliance should not be placed on non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP financial measures are discussed further and reconciled to their applicable GAAP-based financial measures contained in this MD&A beginning on page 49.

On December 16, 2024, we completed the acquisition of Olive & June, LLC ("Olive & June"), an innovative, omni-channel nail care brand. Olive & June products deliver a salon-quality experience at home and include nail polish, press-on nails, manicure and pedicure systems, grooming tools and nail care essentials. The Olive & June brand and products were added to the Beauty & Wellness segment. The total purchase consideration consists of initial cash consideration of $224.7 million, which is net of cash acquired and a favorable post-closing adjustment of $3.9 million, and contingent cash consideration of up to $15.0 million subject to Olive & June's performance during calendar years 2025, 2026, and 2027, payable annually. We incurred pre-tax acquisition-related expenses of $3.0 million during fiscal 2025, which were recognized in SG&A within our consolidated statement of income.

Subsequent to fiscal 2026, on April 14, 2026, we completed the sale of our distribution facility in Southaven, Mississippi for a total sales price of $82.0 million, less costs to sell of $3.8 million. Accordingly, we recognized a gain on the sale of $54.9 million within SG&A during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which was recognized by our Beauty & Wellness segment. We used the proceeds from the sale to repay amounts outstanding under our credit facility.

Since 2019, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative ("USTR") has imposed, and in certain cases subsequently reduced or suspended, additional tariffs on products imported from China. Additionally, the current U.S. presidential administration has promoted and implemented plans to raise tariffs even further and pursue other trade policies intended to restrict imports. Our purchases of products from unaffiliated manufacturers located in China and other regions exposes us to higher costs of doing business from increases in tariffs.

Under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"), the U.S. presidential administration began implementing fentanyl-related IEEPA tariffs ("Fentanyl IEEPA Tariff") and additional tariffs ("Reciprocal IEEPA Tariff") during calendar year 2025. As of April 9, 2025, the U.S. had imposed (i) an aggregate additional 145% tariff on imports from China, consisting of a 20% Fentanyl IEEPA Tariff and 125% Reciprocal IEEPA Tariff and (ii) a global 10% Reciprocal IEEPA Tariff on imports from other countries including Mexico, Vietnam and other U.S. trading partners. The Reciprocal IEEPA Tariff on imports from China was subsequently lowered to 10% effective May 12, 2025, resulting in an aggregate additional 30% tariff. On July 31, 2025, the U.S. president signed an executive order imposing new IEEPA tariffs on a number of U.S. trading partners which became effective on August 7, 2025, including a 25% Fentanyl IEEPA Tariff on imports from Mexico and a 20% and 19% Reciprocal IEEPA Tariff on imports from Vietnam and Thailand, respectively. Effective November 10, 2025, the 10% Reciprocal IEEPA Tariff on imports from China, which was set to expire, was extended to remain in effect through November 10, 2026, and the Fentanyl IEEPA Tariff was reduced from 20% to 10%, reducing the aggregate additional tariff from 30% to 20%. On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that tariffs imposed by the U.S. president under IEEPA were unconstitutional, and the U.S. president subsequently imposed a temporary global 10% Section 122 tariff under the Trade Act of 1974 ("Section 122 Tariff") effective February 24, 2026 through July 24, 2026. As a result, the aggregate additional tariff on imports from China, Vietnam, Mexico and Thailand of 20%, 20%, 25% and 19%, respectively, were replaced by the 10% Section 122 Tariff. Our imports manufactured in Mexico are not impacted since they qualify for duty-free preference under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Further, we benefit from certain exclusions from tariffs as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, which were recently extended to November 9, 2026. We are monitoring regulatory guidance regarding the potential for tariff refunds as a result of the U.S. Supreme Court ruling. As of February 28, 2026, we did not recognize any tariff
refunds in our consolidated financial statements as we were unable to assert loss recovery is probable due to the uncertainty surrounding the tariff refund process and eligibility.

paragraphs: 我們於1968年在德州註冊為Helen of Troy Corporation，並於1994年重組為Helen of Troy Limited，註冊地為百慕達。我們是一家全球領先的消費產品公司，透過多元化的品牌組合，為客戶提供創新的產品與解決方案。我們透過新產品創新、產品品質與具有競爭力的價格，建立了領先的市場地位。我們透過多個品牌進軍市場，其中一些品牌為授權品牌。我們的品牌組合包括OXO、Hydro Flask、Osprey、Vicks、Braun、Honeywell、PUR、Hot Tools、Drybar、Curlsmith、Revlon及Olive & June，以及其他品牌。
我們目前經營兩個應報告分部：
•居家與戶外：提供廣泛的優秀世界級品牌，協助消費者在家內與戶外享受日常生活的樂趣。我們的創新產品用於居家活動，包括食品準備與儲存、烹飪、清潔、整理與飲料服務。我們的戶外性能範疇、隨身食品儲存與飲料容器包括生活方式水合作品、冷卻器與食品儲存解決方案、揹包與旅行用品。此全球分部的銷售主要為線上與實體零售商店，以及透過我們的直營消費者通路。
•美容與健康：為消費者提供廣泛的優秀世界級品牌，用於美容與健康領域。在美容方面，我們透過如髮型電器、理容工具、液體與氣霧個人護理產品及美甲解決方案等產品，協助消費者看起來與感覺更美。在健康方面，我們在您最需要的時候提供高評價的加濕器、體溫計、水與空氣淨化器、加熱器與風扇。此全球分部的銷售主要為線上與實體零售商店、經銷商，以及透過我們的直營消費者通路。
如需更多關於我們淨銷售額、長壽命資產與營運收入的分部與地理資訊，請參閱隨同財務報表附註第17項。
在財務年度2026年，我們進行了重大組織與運營變更，旨在穩定我們的業務。董事會任命了一位新任首席執行官，具備推動我們下一階段價值創造所需的轉型經驗。在這位新領導者之下，我們目前正進行一項全面的戰略優先事項審查，以重新定位本公司，實現持續的銷售與利潤成長，增加市場佔有率，並為所有股東創造優越的長期價值。

我們正在進行業務模式現代化，以符合消費者的需求速度，在快速變化的環境中表現卓越，面對分散的消費者注意力與價值觀的變化。我們的戰略包括以下優先事項：重振品牌與員工、調整組織結構以將消費者置於我們所有行動的中心、強化品牌組合以實現可預測的長期成長，並提高資產效率。根據我們的戰略，我們計畫將重點放在較少但更具影響力的計畫上，包括增加產品創新投資、強化品牌忠誠度，以及推動商業卓越。我們意圖透過有紀律的投資方式，激勵品牌，專注於能產生競爭優勢並為消費者提供產品解決方案與世界級創新機會。在

此外，我們相信以消費者為中心的策略將使我們更深入瞭解消費者，更有效地配置資源，並加快新產品與品牌的上市時間，以抓住最具長期可持續成長潛力的機會。我們預期這將強化我們的品牌組合，為強勁現金流產生提供路徑，以進一步投資於我們的業務。我們持續專注於改善資產負債表的健康與效率，透過優先考量資本支出、優化營運資金，以及處分較不具生產力的資產。雖然我們仍在完成這項戰略調整，但我們已經實施了許多基礎變更，以推動長期表現，並已採取立即行動，我們認為這些行動將加速我們的產品創新、強化我們的市場進入執行、強化現金流，並償還我們的債務。

paragraphs: 本公司的管理層討論與分析（"MD&A"）應與本年度報告的其他部分一併閱讀，包括第 1 項 "業務" 以及第 8 項 "財務資料與補充資料"。本 MD&A 的各個部分包含許多前瞻性陳述，所有這些陳述均基於本公司目前的預期。實際結果可能因多種因素而與預期有重大差異，包括在第 1A 項 "風險因素" 中討論的內容，以及在本 MD&A 之後的 "關於前瞻性陳述資訊" 章節中提及的內容，以及在第 7A 項 "市場風險的定量與定性披露" 中提及的內容。
管理層使用以下關鍵財務指標，其中一些為非 GAAP 指標，如後文進一步說明：淨銷售額、有機業務銷售額、調整後營運毛利及調整後稀釋每股盈餘（"EPS"）。管理層使用這些指標來評估歷史表現，預測未來表現，並與競爭對手進行比較。我們認為這些指標為管理層與投資者提供重要的資訊，有助於理解本公司業務成果與趨勢。

本 MD&A，包括標題為 "營運（損失）收入、營運毛利、調整後營運收入（非 GAAP）及調整後營運毛利（非 GAAP）按分部" 以及 "淨（損失）收入、稀釋（損失）每股盈餘、調整後收入（非 GAAP）及調整後稀釋每股盈餘（非 GAAP）" 的表格，報告營運（損失）收入、營運毛利、淨（損失）收入及稀釋（損失）每股盈餘，不計入併購相關費用、資產減損費用、因巴貝多實施國內公司所得稅立法（"巴貝多稅制改革"）而產生的離散稅務費用、與前任首席執行長（"CEO"）離職相關的成本（"CEO 繼任成本"）、與 EPA 包裝與標籤合規相關的解決費用（"EPA 合規成本"）、因財務重組於財務年度 2025 認可遞延稅資產而產生的過渡性稅務利益，以及財務年度 2026 認可價值減損準備而產生的稅務費用（"無形資產重組"）、重組費用、無形資產攤銷及非現金股票基於報酬費用，如適用。這些指標可能被視為非 GAAP 財務指標，如 SEC Regulation G，Rule 100 所定義。這些表格將這些指標與本公司合併財務報表中對應的 GAAP 財務指標進行對應。我們認為調整後營運收入、調整後營運毛利、調整後收入及調整後稀釋每股盈餘為管理層與投資者提供有用的資訊，以瞭解與本公司財務狀況及營運成果相關的財務與業務趨勢。我們認為這些非 GAAP 財務指標，與本公司根據 GAAP 計算的財務結果結合，為投資者提供額外的視角，以瞭解這些費用與利益對相關收入、毛利及每股盈餘指標的影響。我們也認為這些非 GAAP 指標反映本公司業務的營運表現，並有助於更直接地比較本公司與競爭對手的表現。使用非 GAAP 財務指標的主要限制是，這些指標未反映本公司活動的全部經濟影響。本公司調整後營運收入、調整後營運毛利、調整後收入及調整後稀釋每股盈餘並未根據 GAAP 計算，並非 GAAP 財務指標的替代方案，且可能與其他公司披露的非 GAAP 財務指標計算方式不同。因此，不應過度依賴非 GAAP 財務指標。這些非 GAAP 財務指標在本 MD&A 中進一步討論並與其對應的 GAAP 財務指標進行對應，自第 49 頁開始。

本公司為全球領先的消費產品公司，透過多樣化的品牌組合為客戶提供創新的產品與解決方案。本公司品牌組合包括 OXO、Hydro Flask、Osprey、Vicks、Braun、Honeywell、PUR、Hot Tools、Drybar、Curlsmith、Revlon 及 Olive & June 等。我們透過新產品創新、產品品質及競爭性價格建立了領先的市場地位。截至 2026 年 2 月 28 日，本公司運作兩個應報告分部：居家與戶外及美容與健康。
在財務年度 2026，我們進行了重大組織與運營變革，旨在穩定業務。董事會任命了一位具有轉型經驗的新任首席執行長，以協助推動我們下一階段的價值創造。在這位新領導者之下，我們目前正進行一項全面的戰略優先事項審查，以重新定位本公司，實現持續的營收與利潤成長，增加市場佔有率，並為所有利害關係人創造優越的長期價值。

我們正在進行業務模式現代化，以更快的速度響應消費者需求，並在快速變化的環境中表現卓越，面對分散的消費者注意力與價值觀的變化。我們的戰略包括以下優先事項：重振品牌與員工、調整組織結構，使消費者成為我們一切行動的中心、強化品牌組合以實現可預測的長期成長，並提高資產效率。作為戰略的一部分，我們計劃更加聚焦於少數更具影響力的項目，包括增加產品創新投資、強化品牌忠誠度，並推動商業卓越。我們意圖透過有紀律的投資方式，聚焦於能產生競爭優勢並為消費者提供產品解決方案與世界級創新機會。此外，我們認為以消費者為中心的策略將使我們更深入瞭解消費者，更有效地配置資源，並加快新產品與品牌的上市時間，以抓住長期可持續成長的機會。我們預期這將強化品牌組合，為強勁的現金流產生提供途徑，以進一步投資於本公司業務。我們持續專注於改善資產負債表的健康與效率，透過優先考慮資本支出、優化營運資金，並 monetize 不具生產力的資產。雖然我們仍在完成這項戰略調整，但我們已經實施了許多基礎變革，以推動長期表現，並已採取即時行動，我們認為這些行動將加速產品創新、提高市場推廣執行效率、強化現金流，並償還債務。

於 2024 年 12 月 16 日，我們完成對 Olive & June, LLC（"Olive & June"）之收購，Olive & June 為一創新、全通路美甲護理品牌。Olive & June 產品可於家中提供專業美髮體驗，包含指甲油、貼片指甲、美甲與美足系統、護理工具及美甲護理必需品。Olive & June 品牌與產品已納入 Beauty & Wellness 應報告分部。總購併對價包含初始現金對價 224.7 百萬美元，扣除所取得現金及有利之結案後調整 3.9 百萬美元，以及根據 Olive & June 在 2025、2026 與 2027 年度之表現，最高可達 15.0 百萬美元之條件性現金對價，每年支付。我們於財務年度 2025 期間，因收購相關費用產生前稅前費用 3.0 百萬美元，已於我們合併財務報表之營運及行政費用中列示。
財務年度 2026 之後，於 2026 年 4 月 14 日，我們完成出售位於密西西比州南阿文的配送設施，總銷售價格為 82.0 百萬美元，扣除銷售成本 3.8 百萬美元。因此，我們於財務年度 2027 第一季度內，於營運及行政費用中確認出售收益 54.9 百萬美元，該收益由我們 Beauty & Wellness 應報告分部確認。我們使用出售所得資金償還信用融資之未償還金額。
自 2019 年起，美國貿易代表辦公室（"USTR"）已對從中國進口之產品課徵，並在某些情況下隨後減少或中止，額外關稅。此外，現任美國總統政府已推動並實施計畫，進一步提高關稅，並推行其他貿易政策以限制進口。我們從中國及其他地區之無關聯製造商購買新產品，使我們面臨因關稅提高而導致營運成本增加的風險。

根據國際緊急經濟權力法案（"IEEPA"），美國總統於 2025 年度開始實施與芬太尼相關之 IEEPA 關稅（"Fentanyl IEEPA 關稅"）及額外關稅（"Reciprocal IEEPA 關稅"）。截至 2025 年 4 月 9 日，美國已對從中國進口之產品課徵（i）總計額外 145% 關稅，包含 20% 之 Fentanyl IEEPA 關稅及 125% 之 Reciprocal IEEPA 關稅，以及（ii）對來自其他國家（包括墨西哥、越南及其他美國貿易夥伴）進口產品課徵全球 10% 之 Reciprocal IEEPA 關稅。對中國進口產品之 Reciprocal IEEPA 關稅隨後於 2025 年 5 月 12 日降低至 10%，使總計額外關稅為 30%。於 2025 年 7 月 31 日，美國總統簽署行政命令，對若干美國貿易夥伴課徵新 IEEPA 關稅，該命令於 2025 年 8 月 7 日生效，包含對墨西哥進口產品課徵 25% 之 Fentanyl IEEPA 關稅，以及對越南與泰國進口產品分別課徵 20% 及 19% 之 Reciprocal IEEPA 關稅。自 2025 年 11 月 10 日起，原定於 2025 年 11 月 10 日到期之 10% Reciprocal IEEPA 關稅對中國進口產品已延長至 2026 年 11 月 10 日，且 Fentanyl IEEPA 關稅從 20% 降低至 10%，使總計額外關稅從 30% 降低至 20%。於 2026 年 2 月 20 日，美國最高法院裁定美國總統根據 IEEPA 課徵之關稅違憲，美國總統隨後於 2026 年 2 月 24 日至 2026 年 7 月 24 日間，課徵暫時性全球 10% 之第 122 條關稅（"Section 122 關稅"），根據 1974 年貿易法（"Section 122 關稅"）。因此，中國、越南、墨西哥與泰國進口產品之總計額外關稅 20%、20%、25% 及 19% 已被 10% 之 Section 122 關稅取代。我們從墨西哥製造之進口產品不受影響，因其符合美國-墨西哥-加拿大協議（"USMCA"）之免稅優惠。此外，我們因 COVID-19 疫情而受益於某些關稅豁免，該豁免已延長至 2026 年 11 月 9 日。我們正在監測有關關稅退款之監管指引，以評估美國最高法院裁決後之退款可能性。截至 2026 年 2 月 28 日，我們未在合併財務報表中確認任何關稅退款。
refunds 在我們合併財務報表中未確認，因我們無法主張損失補償為可能，因關稅退款程序及資格之不確定性。

headings: 我們依賴第三方授權的商標，並授權部分商標給第三方以換取 royalty income，若失去這些授權，可能對我們的營業收入與獲利造成重大不利影響。
為成功競爭，我們必須持續開發並推出創新產品，以符合變動中的消費者偏好。
大型客戶可能採取對我們毛利率與營運結果產生不利影響的行動。
我們的營運結果依賴於對幾家大型客戶的銷售，若失去任何主要客戶，或對主要客戶的銷售大幅下降，可能對我們的營業收入與獲利造成重大不利影響。
我們能否及時將產品交付給客戶，並符合客戶的履行標準，取決於多種因素，其中一些因素超出我們的控制範圍。
本公司營運受天氣條件、寒流感季的持續時間與嚴重程度及其他相關因素影響，可能導致營運成果於季與年之間有所變動。
本公司依賴執行長及極少數其他關鍵高階主管來運作業務。若失去任何這些人員，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
法律與法規的變更，包括環境、就業、健康與安全及稅法等，以及遵守這些法律的費用與複雜性，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
對氣候變遷及其他永續議題的關注與期待增加，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響，並損害本公司聲譽。
重大變更或本公司遵守法規、解釋或產品認證要求的情況，可能對本公司營運造成不利影響。
全球關於隱私權與資料安全的法律發展，可能導致本公司業務作法變更、處罰、營運成本增加，或以其他方式損害本公司業務。
本公司業務涉及產品回收、產品責任及其他對本公司提出的聲請，可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 請謹慎考量下列所列風險，以及本年度報告中包含的所有其他資訊，以決定是否投資本公司證券或評估本公司業務。若任何所列風險或其他在本年度報告其他處所提及的事件或情況發生，將可能影響本公司業務、營運結果或財務狀況。因此，本公司普通股的交易價格及您的投資價值可能會顯著下跌。下列所列風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。其他未知或目前認為不重要的風險也可能影響本公司業務。
您應同時參閱第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析」末尾所載有關向前看陳述之資格與限制說明，於「向前看陳述資訊」部分。本公司所作的所有向前看陳述均受下列風險因素所限制。
以下為部分主要風險因素之摘要，詳情請參閱下文。
•本公司美國分銷設施之地理集中性，會增加我們因中斷而影響及時交付產品之風險。
•發生網路安全事件，或本公司或第三方服務供應商未能維護網路安全及保護機密內部或客戶資料之完整性，可能對本公司營運及獲利造成重大不利影響。
•網路安全漏洞、系統過時或本公司中央全球企業資源規劃系統及其他周邊資訊系統運作中斷，可能對本公司營運及獲利造成重大不利影響。
